lead: Combustion is fast, hot and hidden inside metal. To see it, you build an engine with a quartz or sapphire window, light the inside with a laser, and record the scattered light with a high-speed camera. The window engine is not the production engine: its compression ratio, wall temperature and run time differ. Only a few universities teach this chapter, because the hardware is costly. It is used to check spray shape, flame speed, soot and the low-temperature strategies of 6.8.
prereq: You need Unit 3 (flame propagation, spray and air motion), 6.2 for soot incandescence and 6.8 for low-temperature strategies.

sections.h3: An engine you can look into

blocks.text: Optical access means a transparent path for light into the cylinder. A quartz or sapphire window can sit in the cylinder head, the liner or the piston crown. Sapphire is stronger and passes more infrared; quartz is cheaper and good in visible light. The Bowditch extended piston puts a 45° mirror in the piston and a window in the crown, so the camera looks along the cylinder axis. A fully transparent cylinder gives the widest view but weakens the structure. An optical spark plug or injector keeps the same location as the metal part.

An optical engine is not a metal engine. It usually runs a lower compression ratio, has colder or hotter walls, a simplified chamber and a short run limited by window fouling. Fouling is soot and oil on the glass; it dims the signal. Often it fires only a few cycles, so cycle-to-cycle variation is large. The images show mechanism, not production numbers.

sections.h3: Light tuned to a molecule, a droplet or a particle

blocks.text: High-speed direct photography records flame growth and soot incandescence, the glow of hot soot. Schlieren and shadowgraph turn refractive-index gradients into brightness changes, showing density gradients and the flame front. Mie scattering uses a laser and seeded droplets; the droplets scatter strongly and reveal spray shape and penetration. Rayleigh scattering comes from gas molecules; it is weak and gives temperature or concentration after calibration. Laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) excites a chosen molecule and records longer-wavelength emission; it maps fuel, the OH radical or NO. Particle image velocimetry (PIV) uses two short laser pulses and seeded particles; cross-correlation gives the velocity field. Laser Doppler anemometry (LDA) measures the Doppler shift from particles crossing fringes, giving swirl or tumble. Two-colour pyrometry takes soot emission at two wavelengths; the ratio gives soot temperature. Light extinction measures laser light lost across the cylinder and gives soot volume fraction. Endoscopy uses a small borescope in a production engine.

The usual lasers are Nd:YAG at 532 nm, excimer at 308 nm and dye lasers for tunable wavelengths. nm is nanometre, 10<sup>−9</sup> m. A light sheet, not a beam, is what illuminates a plane: cylindrical optics spread the beam into a thin sheet. The flame speed from two frames is S<sub>f</sub> = Δr ÷ Δt, where S<sub>f</sub> is mean flame speed in m/s, Δr is the change in flame radius in m and Δt is the time between frames in s.

examples.question: Two high-speed frames are 0.1 ms apart. Flame radius grows from 8 mm to 12 mm. Engine speed is 1500 rev/min. Find mean flame speed, time for one crank angle degree, and crank angle between frames.
steps: One revolution takes 60 ÷ 1500 = 0.04 s. One crank angle degree takes 0.04 ÷ 360 = 1.11 × 10<sup>−4</sup> s.
examples.answer: Mean flame speed is 40 m/s; one crank angle degree takes 1.11 × 10<sup>−4</sup> s; the frames are 0.9° crank angle apart.
examples.check:
dr = (12 - 8) / 1000
dt = 0.1 / 1000
sf = dr / dt
rpm = 1500
t_deg = 60 / (rpm * 360)
cad = dt / t_deg
print(round(sf, 1))
print(round(t_deg, 6))
print(round(cad, 2))

traps: Quoting an optical-engine flame speed as a production value; lower compression, different walls, a simplified chamber and a short run all shift it.
Forgetting window fouling: soot and oil on quartz dim the signal and limit the run to a few fired cycles.
Treating a line-of-sight image as planar: extinction and direct photography integrate along the beam.
Swapping Mie and Rayleigh: Mie comes from seeded droplets; Rayleigh comes from gas molecules.
Using a beam instead of a sheet for planar imaging: a beam lights a line, a sheet lights a plane.

quiz.q: What does the Bowditch extended piston provide?
quiz.a: A 45° mirror in the extended piston and a window in the crown, so the camera looks along the cylinder axis.

quiz.q: Why is an optical engine not a production engine?
quiz.a: Lower compression ratio, different wall temperatures, simplified chamber, window fouling and few fired cycles shift flame speed and emissions.

quiz.q: A flame radius grows from 10 mm to 14 mm in 0.2 ms. Find mean flame speed.
quiz.a: Δr = 4 mm = 4 × 10<sup>−3</sup> m; Δt = 2 × 10<sup>−4</sup> s; S<sub>f</sub> = 20 m/s.

quiz.q: A Mie image is bright but Rayleigh is weak. Why?
quiz.a: Mie uses strong scattering from seeded droplets; Rayleigh uses weak gas-molecule scattering, so it needs more laser energy and background suppression.

quiz.q: Name two lasers and their wavelengths.
quiz.a: Nd:YAG at 532 nm and excimer at 308 nm; dye lasers are tunable.

quiz.q: Why use a light sheet rather than a beam?
quiz.a: A sheet illuminates a plane, so the camera records a two-dimensional slice; a beam lights only a line.

beyond: Not for the exam. Engine researchers combine PIV, LIF and two-colour pyrometry to validate CFD spray and combustion models, and use endoscopy in production engines for development. Newer work pushes high-speed kHz imaging, tomographic reconstruction and machine-learning post-processing. Search for 'optical IC engine', 'PLIF fuel', 'two-colour pyrometry soot' and 'tomographic PIV engine'.
